# WorkflowBench-S v1: dataset card

**Origin:** original AI-assisted synthetic fixtures generated by `CODE/tools/generate_dataset.py`. The records describe fictional services, teams, archives, policies, facilities, protocols, councils, and retention periods. They are not legal contracts or data from a real institution. No personal information or external copyrighted documents are used.

**Inventory:** 48 one-page native PDFs (106,945 bytes in the recorded run), ten labeled statements per document, eight affirmative relation types and two no-relation statements per document. This gives 480 labeled statements and 384 affirmative graph facts. The native extractor produces 720 total chunks, including headings and disclaimers. The graph contains 432 unique entities. Splits are 30/9/9 documents with 300/90/90 labeled statements. Entity values, including duration values, do not overlap across these splits.

**Gold construction:** the generator writes subject/relation/object records from structured specifications before PDF extraction runs. These are fixture labels, not human adjudication. Templates and algorithms were designed together, so benchmark design bias remains. No inter-annotator agreement was measured. No training model reads labels from the test split.

**Phrasing:** normal splits reuse four template families per affirmative relation. A fifth template for each relation generates 72 additional positive statements from held-out test entities. This stress slice has no negative examples and must not be described as a full open-domain test. Reported stress macro F1 averages the eight positive labels; standard-test macro F1 averages all nine labels.

**Queries:** nine held-out documents each have two literal, two paraphrased, two two-hop and one unanswerable question: 63 in total. Retrieval metrics use 54 answerable queries; abstention is measured on the remaining nine. The corpus index includes all 48 documents; there are no model-training labels in retrieval inference. The handcrafted query planner and question families share the same ontology, creating a deliberately narrow evaluation setting.

**Scans:** four image-only PDFs are derived from the final four held-out native PDFs. Two are clean rasterizations and two add Gaussian blur (0.55) and rotation (0.5 degrees). They contain no native text. They are correlated transformations, not extra independent documents. Actual OCR used Tesseract in one batch. Character and word edit rates are measured after whitespace normalization, retaining case and punctuation.

**Preprocessing:** validate PDF, prefer native page text, OCR only pages with less than 20 alphanumeric characters, normalize Unicode and whitespace, split at English sentence/line boundaries, cap chunks at 100 whitespace tokens, detect typed entity names, and normalize identity by Unicode/whitespace/case. No stemming, fuzzy entity merge, coreference, table reconstruction, or document-level language identification is performed.

**Files:** `raw/` original fixtures; `scans/` image-only samples; `annotations/` gold records and splits; `models/` training outputs; `processed/` actual extracted chunks and triples; `runtime/` local application database and user uploads (Git-ignored).

For a defensible final course experiment, add authorized, independently labeled technical documents, preserve document-level splits, freeze a schema before evaluation, and report failures outside the supported entity grammar. Do not relabel synthetic fixture results as real-document results.
